output.summary: KEP-2392 proposes architectural changes to run the Cloud Controller Manager, moving cloud provider functionality out of Kubernetes core and providing a generic controller manager library for out-of-tree providers. Its status is provisional (from 2021-02-06).
output.rationale: Kubernetes core has seven in-repo cloud provider dependencies, and core is locked against adding new ones, so every change to a provider requires OSS PR approval and a release. The KEP aims to decouple provider code from core releases and to provide a generic controller manager library with feature parity for out-of-tree providers. The sources do not record a final decision beyond the provisional status.

alternatives.option: Side-car process: cloud-interface in tree becomes a GRPC call-out to a side-car
alternatives.why_not: The KEP says the authors believe different providers will want different control loops, so a cloud controller manager is needed anyway, and centralizing the effort there limits the proliferation of new processes across the cluster.

evidence.quote: We are trying to remove any dependencies from Kubernetes Core to any specific cloud provider. Currently we have seven such dependencies.
Have a generic controller manager library available for use by the per cloud provider controller managers.
In addition it should limit the proliferation of new processes across the entire cluster.
Removing and fully deprecating in-tree cloud provider code. That will be coverd in KEP-0013.
